title: Senior Security Engineer, Detection & Response
description:
Senior Security Engineer - Detection & Response

Department: Engineering

Location: Toronto (hybrid)

Compensation: CA$150K – CA$245K • Offers Equity • Multiple Ranges

Employment Type: FullTime

EvenUp is on a mission to close the justice gap using technology and AI. We empower personal injury lawyers and victims to get the justice they deserve. Our products enable law firms to secure faster settlements, higher payouts, and better outcomes for victims injured through no fault of their own in vehicle collisions, accidents, natural disasters, and more.

We are one of the fastest-growing vertical SaaS companies in history, and we are just getting started. EvenUp is backed by top VCs, including Bessemer Venture Partners, Bain Capital Ventures, SignalFire, and Lightspeed. We are looking to expand our team with talented, driven, and collaborative individuals who seek to have a lasting impact. Learn more at www.evenuplaw.com.

Life as an Engineer at EvenUp 🎥

Security at EvenUp is still early enough to shape — and detection and response is the part we're building next, from the ground up.

We're looking for a hands-on Senior Security Engineer to build our detection and response program: the telemetry pipelines, the SIEM, the detection content, and the incident response muscle behind them. You won't inherit a SOC — you'll design one.

This isn't a role where you'll stare at a queue of vendor alerts. The threats that matter most to us don't come out of any box: they live in our own applications and data flows, and detecting them means partnering with the engineers who build those systems. We believe security should accelerate the business, not slow it down. If you're excited about treating detection as an engineering discipline, we'd love to chat.

Why this role is exciting

  • Build the program, not just the rules: select the SIEM, design the telemetry architecture, and write the first generation of detections; your technical decisions become the foundation.

  • Detect what actually matters: focus on highest-stakes risks unique to our business, like sensitive data moving to the wrong place, misuse of internal systems, and exposure of health information, as generic detection content cannot address these.

  • Detection as code: detections are written, version-controlled, tested, and reviewed like software.

  • Own incident response: define how EvenUp responds to incidents, including playbooks, tabletop exercises, and post-incident reviews.

  • Direct the vendors, don't answer to them: when using managed providers for 24/7 coverage, you set the requirements, escalation logic, and quality standards.

What You'll Do

  • Build Our Detection Platform: Lead SIEM evaluation and implementation, design log ingestion and routing pipelines, and make deliberate cost/retention trade-offs across hot search and long-term archive.

  • Engineer High-Signal Detections: Develop and tune detection content across cloud, identity, endpoint, SaaS, and application telemetry — with an emphasis on business-logic detections built on our own products' audit events.

  • Define the Telemetry Contract: Partner with Engineering and DevOps to specify what our applications and infrastructure must log — the audit events that make our most important risks detectable in the first place.

  • Lead Incident Response: Build and maintain IR playbooks and runbooks, coordinate response during security events, run the annual tabletop exercise, and drive post-incident reviews that actually change things.

  • Detect Data Exposure: Partner with internal teams to detect sensitive data moving where it shouldn't — including PHI — across applications, endpoints, and SaaS.

  • Manage 24/7 Coverage: Define requirements for and direct our managed detection partners, own escalation procedures, and continuously raise the bar on what "monitored" means.

What We Look For

  • 5+ years in security operations, detection engineering, or incident response, including experience building (not just running) a detection and response capability at a startup or high-growth technology company.

  • Hands-on experience implementing or significantly maturing a SIEM, including custom log sources and detection content — not just operating one that was handed to you.

  • Strong detection engineering skills: writing detections in Python, SQL, or a rules DSL, managing them in version control, and measuring their quality.

  • Real incident response experience — you've led investigations, written the playbooks, and run the retros.

  • Experience with cloud-native telemetry (AWS/GCP/Azure control plane, identity providers, endpoint, SaaS audit logs).

  • Strong programming or automation skills (Python preferred); comfort building integrations and response automation.

  • Experience partnering directly with software engineers to instrument applications for security visibility is a strong plus.

  • Familiarity with securing or monitoring AI/LLM-powered systems is a strong plus.

  • Experience working with MDR/MSSP providers — and opinions about what they're good and bad at.

  • A builder mentality — you'd rather engineer the alert away than triage it forever.

  • Relevant security certifications (GIAC/GCIA/GCIH, CISSP, etc.) are a plus, but practical engineering experience matters more.

This is a hybrid role, with an expectation of being in our Toronto office three days per week.

title: Serviceingenjör
description:

Service Manager

Vi undanber oss vänligen direktkontakt med bemannings- och rekryteringsföretag samt säljare av ytterligare platsannonser.

Vi ser fram emot att läsa din ansökan i PDF-format. Vi arbetar med löpande urval vilket innebär att tjänsten kan komma att tillsättas före sista ansökningsdag. title: Senior Software Engineer, Java Backend
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Java Backend based in Brazil.

This role offers the opportunity to engineer mission-critical backend services supporting large-scale IT operations across millions of managed endpoints and servers. You will design, develop, and evolve highly available software within a distributed cloud environment. Working alongside experienced backend, UI, and systems engineers, you will contribute to complex services involving real-time communication, session management, and reliable data flows. You will have significant influence over architecture, scalability, performance, and long-term maintainability. The position combines hands-on development with technical leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and mentorship. It is well suited to an experienced Java engineer who enjoys solving complex distributed-systems challenges at scale.

Accountabilities

  • Lead the design and development of large-scale backend applications and services, delivering reliable, maintainable, and high-quality software.
  • Design and implement scalable solutions using Java and modern backend engineering practices within a distributed cloud environment.
  • Influence critical architectural decisions, balancing scalability, performance, technical debt, maintainability, and business requirements.
  • Develop and improve services supporting high-availability, client-server communication, asynchronous processing, and real-time distributed workflows.
  • Work on backend infrastructure responsible for connection negotiation, session state, communication reliability, and data flows across geographically distributed environments.
  • Identify and resolve complex system-design and performance challenges, including large-scale datastore bottlenecks and caching requirements.
  • Take ownership of technical initiatives from conception through delivery, proactively identifying challenges and driving improvements based on customer and support feedback.
  • Collaborate closely with engineers, product stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align technical decisions and deliver effective solutions.
  • Promote quality-first engineering practices, including robust testing, reliability, maintainability, and performance optimization.
  • Mentor junior engineers, share technical knowledge, and contribute to engineering standards and best practices across projects.
  • Support additional technical initiatives and responsibilities that contribute to the success and evolution of the engineering organization.

    • A quality-focused mindset and commitment to building reliable, scalable, and maintainable software.

title: Nursing Project Manager - CSC
description:
Nursing Project Manager – Crisis Solutions Center (CDF & CDIS)

Schedule: Mon-Fri, 9am - 5pm with some variable/on-call hours required

Insurance Benefits: Medical (no premiums/payroll deductions for employee coverage), Dental, Life, Long-term Disability

Other Benefits: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Flexible Spending Account (FSA), ORCA card subsidy, Paid Time Off (34 days per year), Retirement Plan


Please note: This position is being recruited in advance, with the selected candidate expected to begin employment in approximately September 2026.


About DESC:

Recognized nationally as an innovator and leader in developing solutions to homelessness, DESC is a social services organization, supportive housing operator, and licensed behavioral health treatment provider focused on meeting the needs of people experiencing long-term homelessness and living with complex behavioral health and other medical conditions. Approximately 3,000 people are actively receiving services from DESC at any given point in time. Our vision is a community where all people are shown compassion, treated with dignity, and everyone has a safe, stable, and affordable place to call home.


DESC operates five shelter/emergency housing programs,19 permanent supportive housing facilities with over 1,750 units, several hundred additional scattered site apartments, and a range of behavioral health services including outpatient mental health and substance use disorder treatment, residential crisis stabilization, street outreach, mobile crisis response, and treatment for opioid use disorder.


Job Definition:
The Nursing Project Manager provides leadership and operational oversight for all program functions at DESC’s Crisis Diversion Facility (CDF) and Crisis Diversion Interim Services (CDIS), with a focus on integrating medical, nursing, and case management services into cohesive and effective daily operations. Together with the Clinical Project Manager, this role forms a unified leadership team responsible for the overall functioning of the Crisis Solutions Center (CSC). The two Project Managers share accountability for program outcomes, staff coordination, and the delivery of consistent, recovery-oriented, trauma-informed, and harm-reduction–based care.


The Nursing Project Manager ensures that medical and nursing practices are embedded within the larger operational framework of the program and that clinical and case management workflows are fully aligned. In addition to clinical leadership, this position carries shared responsibility for floor operations, staffing, facility coordination, and maintaining a safe and therapeutic environment. The Nursing Project Manager supervises the Nurse Supervisor, may also supervise Clinical Supervisors, and provides coverage supervision for Registered Nurses.


This position reports directly to the Senior Program Manager (SPM) while also receiving supplemental supervision from DESC’s Director of Nursing and collaborating closely with the CSC Senior Medical Lead. The role participates in Nursing Department trainings, retreats, and professional development activities to ensure alignment with agency-wide nursing practice standards. With a broader scope of responsibility than the Clinical Project Manager, this position carries expanded authority over medical and operational systems within the CSC, while serving as an equal partner in shared decision-making and strategic direction for the program’s overall success.


Major Duties and Responsibilities

Program Operations & Supervision

  • Provide direct clinical and administrative supervision of the Nurse Supervisor, and as assigned, Registered Nurses and Clinical Supervisors as needed.
  • Share oversight of case management services in collaboration with the Clinical Project Manager to ensure that client support plans are fully integrated with nursing and medical services.
  • Maintain strong presence on program floors to monitor daily operations, client flow, and staff performance, intervening as needed to support safe and effective service delivery.
  • Oversee scheduling, staffing ratios, and coverage to ensure continuous nursing, medical, and integrated case management support across both units.
  • Provide on-call support as part of a rotating leadership schedule to ensure continuous after-hours coverage for emergent operational and clinical issues.
  • Conduct performance evaluations and maintain supporting documentation in confidential personnel files.
  • Train, coach, and mentor nursing and case management staff in crisis intervention, engagement, and integrated care practices.
  • Ensure DESC and CSC program values are fully incorporated into all aspects of floor operations, including harm reduction, trauma-informed care, and recovery-oriented practices.

Clinical Accountability & Service Delivery

  • Oversee medication management systems, including monitoring and administration of psychiatric medications in a manner consistent with client needs and safety.
  • Coordinate interdisciplinary care planning with the Clinical Project Manager to align case management and medical interventions.
  • Conduct regular assessments of client medical and psychiatric needs, ensuring appropriate linkage to primary and specialty care.
  • Provide client education on medical and psychiatric conditions, treatment options, and recovery strategies.
  • Ensure compliance with licensing, DEA, and DOH regulations relevant to medication management and clinical care.
  • Participate in clinical reviews, psychiatric consultations, and multidisciplinary case conferences.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

  • Monitor adherence to all contract, regulatory, and licensing requirements (HCA, WAC, DOH, King County).
  • Lead quality assurance and quality improvement initiatives related to nursing and medical services.
  • Coordinate data collection and reporting requirements with DESC’s Information Systems team and funders.
  • Implement best practices in integrated behavioral health and medical care.
  • Participate in agency-wide Nursing Department trainings, retreats, and initiatives to ensure program alignment with DESC nursing standards.

External Collaboration & Community Relations

  • Serve as point person for coordination with external healthcare providers, hospitals, urgent care, and specialty care.
  • Represent DESC in community healthcare collaborations, advocating for integrated medical/behavioral health care for CSC clients.
  • Maintain collaborative relationships with referral sources, detox facilities, shelters, and emergency medical providers.
  • Promote positive relationships with the surrounding neighborhood.

Safety & Crisis Response

  • Participate in verbal de-escalation and physical interventions during client crises, modeling calm and confident leadership.
  • Ensure nursing and medical staff are trained and competent in crisis response.
  • Provide building security as needed and support staff in maintaining a safe and therapeutic environment.
  • Respond to medical emergencies as needed, including performing CPR or administering basic first aid until additional medical assistance arrives.

Administrative Responsibilities

  • Participate in staff recruitment, hiring, training, and retention efforts.
  • Ensure nursing protocols, policies, and workflows are updated and consistently applied.
  • Manage operational needs including supply chain, vendor coordination, and medical equipment.
  • Maintain compliance with DESC policies, procedures, and collective bargaining agreements.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to support the effective operation of CSC.

title: Head of Digital Transformation & ICT
description:
Inland Fisheries Ireland (IFI) has an exciting opportunity for an experienced Head of Digital Transformation and ICT to lead the organisation's ICT strategy, operations, and digital transformation agenda. The Head of Digital Transformation and ICT is a senior role within the ICT function of IFI and will serve as a member of the IFI Executive Leadership Team (ELT).

The ideal candidate will be a role model for strategic leadership, operational excellence, creating a high-performance culture and building strong stakeholder relationships. IFI is seeking candidates that are ‘thought leaders’, keen to challenge, pioneer change and enthuse others to deliver on our mission and vision, in line with our values.

This post will be responsible for strategically leading a team in the delivery of digital and technology architecture and solutions, operational business objectives, annual business and work plans and implementation of an organisation-wide Digital and Technology strategy. Cooperation and successful collaboration with other Heads of Function and operational Directors is a vital component in this role.

ABOUT US

Inland Fisheries Ireland is the state agency responsible for protecting, managing and conserving Ireland's inland fisheries and sea angling resources. More information can be found by visiting our website.

OUR VISION, MISSION & VALUES

Vision

To place the inland fisheries resource in the best sustainable position possible for the benefit of future generations.

Mission

To protect, manage and conserve Ireland’s inland fisheries and sea angling resources and to maximise their sustainability and natural biodiversity.

Values

  • We work collaboratively with professionalism

  • We are open, transparent and accountable

  • We act with respect and integrity

  • We are committed to stewardship and sustainability

THE ROLE

The Head of Digital Transformation & ICT will be responsible for the development and implementation of a digital transformation agenda and overseeing the day-to-day ICT operations at Inland Fisheries Ireland (IFI). Working collaboratively with key stakeholders internally and externally the Head of Digital Transformation & ICT will ensure the delivery of a Digital Strategy for IFI. They will lead on achieving a full enterprise architecture, bringing together an integrated Digital Strategy with the support of all functions within the organisation.

The role will have expert oversight of organisational data quality, security and systems in a manner that supports the business and new approach contained in the IFI Statement of Strategy 2026 – 2030 and annual workplans. The role will also involve the preparation and management of ICT budgets, in line with approved business plans and financial guidelines. The Head of Digital Transformation & ICT will monitor performance, report on key ICT activities and metrics, as required, and ensure that ICT governance, compliance, and best practice standards are maintained across the organisation.

This is a challenging and rewarding senior public sector role for a dynamic individual to lead on the transformation of a State Agency towards an efficient and effective service delivery model for staff and an extensive range of external stakeholders. IFI are therefore seeking an impactful strategic leader, with a track record of achievement and an ethos of customer focus and continuous improvement to deliver high-quality, progressive and efficient services through the development of a high-performing team.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support and advise the Chief Executive Officer in the discharge of their functions ensuring technology is a true enabler.

  • Participate in the executive leadership of the Agency, provide direct support and advice to the Board and its Sub-Committees, and contribute to the development and operational delivery of IFI’s Statement of Strategy 2026-2030.

  • Manage significant external and internal stakeholders and maintain positive relationships with all stakeholders.

  • Oversee the IFI technology infrastructure estate, maintaining optimal resilience and security, commensurate with the expectations of the organisation.

  • Proactively lead on the implementation of a full enterprise architecture that optimises fragmented processes, information and technology into an integrated environment at IFI, facilitating effective decision making and change implementation.

  • Engage with key stakeholders to develop and implement a Digital Strategy for IFI that supports delivery of the Statement of Strategy 2026-2030 and meets customer needs across all parts of the business.

  • Lead on the delivery of the Digital Strategy and multi-year plans, continuously re-evaluating to ensure alignment with organisational priorities and the delivery of business value.

  • Ensure the transformation of the enabling corporate functions through the selection and implementation of modern digital technology solutions that will radically improve the efficiency of these functions and the internal employee experience.

  • Develop a suite of Technology metrics and KPIs which will demonstrate the function’s ‘value add’ to the business and provide regular performance reports to the Digital & ICT Board Sub-Committee and the Board.

  • Build the capacity and capability of the Digital Transformation & ICT Division and develop a high-performance team culture, through workforce planning, effective performance and development planning and personnel management.

  • Develop and manage ICT budgets, in line with agreed business plans and within pre-assigned limits. Manage significant capital and operating expenditure, tracking expenditure, ensuring optimal use of resources and delivering value for money.

  • Ensure robust governance processes associated with the Digital Transformation & ICT function are in place, including oversight of programme delivery through key governance mechanisms and the effective management of risk.

  • Oversee the sourcing and management of best-in-class partners and vendors, in compliance with public procurement guidelines.

  • Engage with external stakeholders to learn from best practices and international developments. Build strong working relationships and influence across the wider Government and Public Service technology leadership sphere, developing opportunities for collaboration and integration.

  • Ensure all Service Level Agreements and Key Performance Indicators (KPI’s) are clearly communicated and delivered.

  • Ensure that ICT initiatives contribute effectively to environmental sustainability and digital innovation within the public sector context.

  • Ensure compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and data governance policies, promoting a culture of data security and privacy across the organisation.

  • Represent IFI nationally and internationally as required and liaise with relevant external bodies, agencies and organisations.

  • Undertake all other duties and responsibilities as may be assigned from time to time by the CEO or nominee.

KNOWLEDGE, QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

Essential

  • A recognised third-level qualification, at a minimum of NFQ Level 8, in Computer Science, IT or a related discipline.

  • Significant Information Technology experience at a senior level in a complex organisation, including senior stakeholder engagement while managing resources and risk at an executive leadership level.

  • A full clean Category B driving licence that is valid in Ireland.

  • Significant vendor management and financial budget management experience – capital and operating expenditure.

  • Project management experience, including the use of a project management methodology.

  • Demonstrated capacity to think and act strategically and innovatively, and shape long-term direction through informed digital and operational planning.

  • Proven ability to deliver utilising all available resources and securing the best outcomes based on objectives.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead and develop staff through effective coaching and collaboration, fostering high-performing teams that deliver against challenging objectives.

  • Clear ability to communicate in a manner that is understandable to non-technical stakeholders.

Desirable

  • Experience in digital transformation or leading ICT transformation programmes in a public sector or regulated environment

  • Understanding of public sector procurement regulations and ICT frameworks (OGP or EU procurement).

  • Strong understanding of ICT governance, risk, and compliance in a state or semi-state body.

  • Experience in managing an application development function using a variety of structured development functions.

  • Strong understanding of business process optimisation, with exposure to emerging technologies and demonstrable experience in using applications to enhance organisational performance and customer service.

  • A clear understanding of IFI’s legal, technical, and operational environment and processes.

  • Excellent analytical skills and proven ability to solve problems effectively

  • A demonstrated ability to think clearly, meet tight deadlines, and deliver results under pressure.

REMUNERATION

The salary scale for the position is at the level of Principal Officer (Head of Function) as it applies in Inland Fisheries Ireland, This is a 7-point scale including two long service increments (LSI’s):
Point 1 €106,926.15; Point 2 €111,513.12; Point 3 €116,069.35; Point 4 €120,660.71; Point 5 €124,529.33; Point 6 (LSI 1) €128,542.93; Point 7 €132,549.95

(IFI Principal Officer (Head of Function) Salary Scale as of 01/06/2026).


Candidates should note that new appointments will be at the minimum of the scale and the rate of remuneration will not be subject to negotiation and may be adjusted from time to time in line with Government pay policy. Candidates should note that different salary terms and conditions may apply if, immediately prior to appointment, the appointee is/was a serving civil or public servant.

LOCATION

This role will be based at IFI’s office in Citywest Business Campus, Dublin D24 CK66.

TENURE

The term of appointment for the role will be permanent and pensionable. The appointee will be required to serve a nine-month probationary period.

ANNUAL LEAVE

The role offers a generous annual leave entitlement of 30 days per annum (pro-rata), supporting a positive work-life balance.

BENEFITS

  • Modern, accessible Dublin HQ with many transport options.

  • Inland Fisheries Ireland is proud to offer a hybrid working model for this role, subject to business requirements.

APPLICATIONS & SELECTION PROCESS

A cover letter and up to date Curriculum Vitae should be submitted by 5.00 pm on Wednesday, 16th September 2026.

Late applications will not be processed.

Shortlisting will be based on information provided in the Cover Letter and CV.

Canvassing will disqualify.

Any questions regarding this opportunity should be directed to IFI’s Head of People and Culture, Éilis Mernagh by email at Eilis.Mernagh@fisheriesireland.ie

Inland Fisheries Ireland is an equal opportunities employer.

title: Per Diem Psychiatric ARNP - Crisis Solutions Center (CSC)
description:
Shift: Variable - no earlier than 8am, no later than 7pm

Benefits: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Safe & Sick Time, Retirement Plan

Union Representation: This position is a part of a union and is represented by SEIU Healthcare 1199NW.


About DESC:

Recognized nationally as an innovator and leader in developing solutions to homelessness, DESC is a social services organization, supportive housing operator, and licensed behavioral health treatment provider focused on meeting the needs of people experiencing long-term homelessness and living with complex behavioral health and other medical conditions. Approximately 3,000 people are actively receiving services from DESC at any given point in time. Our vision is a community where all people are shown compassion, treated with dignity, and everyone has a safe, stable, and affordable place to call home.


DESC operates five shelter/emergency housing programs, 19 permanent supportive housing facilities with over 1,750 units, several hundred additional scattered site apartments, and a range of behavioral health services including outpatient mental health and substance use disorder treatment, residential crisis stabilization, street outreach, mobile crisis response, and treatment for opioid use disorder.


JOB DEFINITION:

The Psychiatric ARNP is responsible for providing psychiatric evaluations, diagnosis & treatment; crisis stabilization; medication prescription; recommending rehabilitation services, and coordination with community providers as necessary.


JOB DEFINITION:

The Psychiatric ARNP is a member of a multi-disciplinary team and is responsible for providing psychiatric evaluations, diagnosis & treatment; crisis stabilization; medication prescription; recommending rehabilitation services, and coordination with community providers as necessary. In conjunction with other psychiatric and management staff, this position has clinical responsibility for monitoring participant treatment and staff delivery of clinical services, assuring compliance with all local, state and federal laws and relevant contract and procedure requirements associated with operations within DESC.


Services will be provided in participants' home and community at least 75% of the time which includes travel time to perform services. In conjunction with the project manager, team leader, Nursing Supervisor, psychiatrist and Medical Director, this position has overall clinical responsibility for monitoring participant treatment and staff delivery of clinical services. All members of the team are expected to work with participants in a variety of shared functions. This team is designed to work with individuals who have experienced long durations or multiple episodes in psychiatric hospitalizations and/or residential mental health treatment. Individuals served experience chronic or multiple episodes of severe mental illness, co-occurring substance use disorders and possibly homelessness. These individuals have either been unable or unwilling to participate and succeed in traditional treatment settings. Therefore, it is critical that the members of this team work together in a collaborative manner that eliminates the traditional treatment borders and barriers.


MAJOR DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Coordinate client care with a multi-disciplinary team of social workers/case managers, chemical dependency professionals, psychiatric nurses, peer counselors, employment specialists and other mental health staff within the PACT team.
  • Perform full psychiatric evaluations and provide treatment and recommendations as appropriate, at DESC sites and in the community, as needed by program and individual need.
  • Diagnose the nature and extent of mental and/or substance-related disorders by reviewing the client’s clinical record, requesting and reviewing known medical/psychiatric documentation, coordination with other providers, and evaluating the client's current physical and psychological condition.
  • Coordinate all psychiatric services provided with Program management, Medical Director, nursing and other management staff.
  • PACT always has a provider on-call who is available for consultation with other staff as well as Emergency Departments, first-responders, and other medical providers.
  • Maintain compliance with all related licensing, DEA, and other regulations.
  • Conduct all work within principles of the Recovery model.
  • Evaluate clients and advise course of treatment. Respond to emergency situations as needed.
  • Refer and advocate for clients to consult with a primary care physician on a regular basis. When appropriate, refer clients to other specialists.
  • For all clients receiving medication treatment, conduct a face to face evaluation at least every 90 days or other schedule as related regulations or contract terms change.
  • Document all client contacts and pertinent information according to agency, County, and State requirements within stated time lines. Provide treatment in compliance with relevant RSN policies and procedures and all local, state and federal requirements.
  • In coordination with the Medical Director and Psychiatrist, participate in clinical program planning, matters of regulatory compliance for medical staff, and other issues relating to delivery and integration of psychiatric care.
  • Actively participate in staff meetings and in-service trainings.
  • Provide weekly psychiatric consultation to treatment teams and individual consultation as time allows.
  • Provide education to clinical teams and individually as opportunity and need presents.
  • Demonstrate the ability to work effectively under supervision, as part of a multi-disciplinary team, and independently, when necessary.
  • Take initiative to meet the changing needs of community mental health treatment.
  • Participate in verbal de-escalation and physical interventions in emergent situations and be willing and able to assist other staff as needed to maintain a safe and secure environment.
  • Other duties as assigned.

title: Executive Director
description:
Executive Director


Elyson | Katy, TX

$105,000–$115,000 + Up to 10% Annual Bonus + Comprehensive Benefits + 16 Paid Holidays

Hiring range based on experience, skills, and qualifications.


Collaboration. Authenticity. Connection. Balance.


At Cohere, we believe community is the most valuable amenity.


We do more than manage communities—we help create places where people connect, belong, and thrive. By partnering with some of the nation’s most innovative master-planned communities, we create places residents are proud to call home and where meaningful relationships flourish.


We’re looking for an Executive Director to serve as the senior leader of Elyson, one of Texas’ premier master-planned communities. Spanning more than 3,600 acres and continuing to grow toward approximately 8,000 homes at buildout, Elyson is a complex, highly amenitized community with expanding neighborhoods, recreation centers, pools, fitness facilities, parks, trails, lakes, sports courts, community programming, and commercial development.


This is not a traditional community management position. The Executive Director will have responsibility for the overall leadership, strategy, operations, financial performance, governance, and resident experience of the community, while partnering closely with the Board of Directors, Developer, Cohere leadership, residents, vendors, and other community stakeholders.


As Elyson continues to grow, this leader will help shape how the community operates at scale—building strong teams and systems, anticipating future needs, protecting the community’s long-term vision, and ensuring a consistently exceptional experience for the people who call Elyson home.


If you’re an experienced community executive who can balance strategic leadership with operational excellence, build credibility with sophisticated stakeholders, and lead a large-scale community through continued growth, we’d love to meet you.


Why People Choose Cohere


The best communities are built by people who feel supported, valued, and empowered to do their best work. That’s why we invest in benefits, time away, and professional growth that help our team members thrive both personally and professionally.


Highlights Include:

  • Medical coverage available on your first day
  • Employer-paid dental coverage
  • Vision coverage
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Employer-paid Life Insurance, AD&D, and Long-Term Disability coverage
  • Pet insurance options
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health, financial, legal, and family support resources
  • Travel assistance and identity theft protection
  • Complimentary will preparation services
  • Generous paid time off
  • 16 paid holidays each year, including a Birthday Day and Volunteer Day, in addition to PTO
  • Professional development and growth opportunities

What You’ll Do


Lead the Community

  • Serve as the senior leader and central point of accountability for Elyson, providing strategic direction across community operations, governance, resident experience, facilities, engagement, and community standards.
  • Translate the Board’s, Developer’s, and community’s long-term vision into clear priorities, operating strategies, and measurable outcomes.
  • Anticipate the needs of a rapidly growing master-planned community and develop the people, processes, systems, and resources necessary to support continued growth.
  • Represent Elyson with professionalism and credibility as a visible leader and trusted resource for residents, Board members, the Developer, community partners, and other stakeholders.

Build and Lead a High-Performing Team

  • Lead, coach, and develop a multidisciplinary team that includes Directors, Managers, Coordinators, and other community professionals.
  • Establish clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards while creating an inclusive, collaborative culture.
  • Build organizational systems and leadership practices that allow the team to operate effectively as the size and complexity of the community continue to increase.
  • Foster strong cross-functional collaboration across community operations, engagement, standards, facilities, finance, and other areas.

Oversee Governance and Stakeholder Relationships

  • Partner closely with the Board of Directors and Developer to execute community priorities and provide sound operational and strategic guidance.
  • Oversee Board governance processes, reporting, presentations, records, resolutions, policies, and implementation of Board directives.
  • Interpret and apply governing documents while working collaboratively with legal counsel, committees, residents, and other stakeholders.
  • Build productive relationships grounded in trust, transparency, sound judgment, and a shared commitment to the community’s long-term success.

Drive Financial and Operational Performance

  • Maintain executive oversight of association budgets, financial performance, cash flow, budget variances, annual audits, long-range planning, and project buildout budgets.
  • Apply strong financial judgment to community priorities, capital needs, operational decisions, and long-term planning.
  • Oversee facilities, landscape operations, community standards, design review, vendor relationships, contracts, and risk management.
  • Develop and monitor strategic plans, operating goals, performance measures, and organizational priorities.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen processes, improve service delivery, increase efficiency, and prepare the organization for future growth.

Champion the Community Experience

  • Ensure decisions and operations support an exceptional resident experience and reinforce Elyson’s vision and brand promise.
  • Promote meaningful connection through thoughtful community engagement, communication, programming, and relationship-building.
  • Partner with development and marketing teams to bring the Community Life perspective into future planning, community design, and new initiatives.
  • Serve as a composed and solutions-oriented leader when navigating complex resident, stakeholder, operational, or governance matters.

What We’re Looking For

CACI has an exciting opportunity for an Electronics Engineer-Modeling to support the engineering analysis and modeling of foreign RF systems and signal processing.

Document findings in modeling tools, databases, and written assessments

• Model maintenance and development.

Qualifications:

• Experience in Verification and Validation of models • Knowledge of RF systems and RF physics, waves, antennas, radars.

• 5+ years of relevant experience.

title: Full Stack Developer
description:
Be visionary

Teledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research.

We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins.

Job Description

Teledyne CARIS is a global leader in the design and production of geospatial software solutions for the hydrographic, marine, and maritime industries. As part of Teledyne Technologies, we develop advanced data management and production systems used by hydrographic offices, ports, and maritime authorities worldwide.

Developer for Cartographic Production Tools

We are currently seeking a highly motivated developer to join our HPD team in Fredericton NB. This role focuses on the development and evolution of our Hydrographic Production Database (HPD), a production system used around the world for managing, validating, and producing marine charting data.

The successful candidate will contribute to database design, query development, and backend services, working with complex schemas and complex geospatial datasets. A strong foundation in relational databases, API development, and data-driven systems is essential. Experience with PostgreSQL is highly desirable, and Oracle experience is also considered a strong asset.

What’s in it for you?

Technical challenge – Collaborate with domain experts and experienced developers in hydrography.

A great place to work and grow – You will enjoy the relaxed and friendly atmosphere of a company with a long tradition in the Maritimes. We have a deep bench of technical staff that you can learn from and are regularly working with customers who are leaders in their industry.

Global opportunities – Contribute to software used by hydrographic offices and maritime organizations worldwide.

Meaningful outcome – Build systems that directly support safe navigation and maritime operations.

Your Role in Plain Text:

  • Build new features using C++ on using our application layer

  • Develop and optimize SQL queries, views, and stored procedures

  • Build and maintain backend services and APIs for accessing and managing HPD data

  • Work with PostgreSQL or Oracle for data storage, querying, and optimization

  • Support data ingestion, validation, and transformation processes

  • Contribute to data modeling aligned with hydrographic standards (e.g., S-57, S-100)

  • Collaborate with developers, domain experts, and product owners in an agile environment

  • Participate in performance tuning, troubleshooting, and debugging of data-related issues

  • Contribute to automated testing and continuous integration practices

  • Present new features and improvements in internal demos

To be successful in this role, we would love if you have:

  • Bachelor’s degree or master’s in computer science or engineering

  • 4+ years of relevant experience as a backend or full stack developer

  • Strong experience with relational databases and SQL

  • Experience developing APIs (e.g., RESTful services) and integrating with backend systems

  • Experience with backend development in C++

  • Fluency in English

Knowledge of the following technologies is an asset

PostgreSQL, Oracle, Python, API design and development (REST, JSON), Geospatial data formats and standards (S-57, S-100, GIS concepts), Database performance tuning and indexing strategies, Subversion, Git, Jira

Other skills

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, especially with data-intensive systems

  • Attention to detail and commitment to data quality and integrity

  • Effective collaboration and communication skills

  • Interest in geospatial or hydrographic domains

  • Desire to learn domain-specific standards and technologies

Why Join Teledyne CARIS?

  • Work with industry-leading technology used around the world

  • Engage with global clients across government, defense, and commercial sectors

  • Opportunities for international travel and professional growth

  • Collaborative and innovative team environment

What happens next

Teledyne and all of our employees are committed to conducting business with the highest ethical standards. We require all employees to comply with all applicable laws, regulations, rules and regulatory orders. Our reputation for honesty, integrity and high ethics is as important to us as our reputation for making innovative sensing solutions.

title: Lead, Brand & Design
description:
Lead, Brand & Design

Location: Delhi / Gurgaon

Company: Lenskart

�� Mission Brief: Building the Next-Generation AI-First Creative Engine

You will architect and operationalize Lenskart's transformation into a next-generation, AI-native creative powerhouse—a brand that produces world-class creative at exponential speed and scale. Your mission is to fundamentally reimagine how a global consumer brand creates, produces, and delivers visual storytelling across every touchpoint: films, digital assets, packaging, retail, social, campaigns, and experiences.

This isn't about managing designers or adopting AI tools incrementally. You're redefining the creative stack itself—building the systems, workflows, technology infrastructure, and human capabilities that allow Lenskart to produce 10x more creative output with the same or fewer resources, while maintaining (or elevating) creative excellence.

You'll bridge the gap between artistic vision and technological innovation. As AI democratizes creative production, you'll position Lenskart not as a follower, but as a creative technology leader that uses AI as an amplifier for human creativity, not a replacement. Your creative teams will operate like a distributed creative studio powered by intelligent systems, real-time collaboration, and generative tools—delivering campaign-ready assets in days instead of weeks.

This is a foundational role that shapes how the world experiences Lenskart's visual identity for the next decade.

�� Core Mandate: AI-Powered Creative Transformation 1. Creative Platform & Technology Architecture (The Builder's Focus)

AI-First Creative Ecosystem Design: Own the strategic vision, architecture, and deployment of Lenskart's proprietary AI-native creative production platform. This includes integrated systems for:

● Intelligent asset generation (images, videos, motion graphics, 3D)

● AI-assisted creative ideation and concept development

● Automated workflows for editing, color grading, localization, and asset optimization ● Generative tools for design variations, rapid prototyping, and A/B testing ● Cross-platform optimization and adaptive creative delivery

Creative Tech Stack Strategy: Evaluate, integrate, and operationalize emerging creative technologies—generative AI (image/video/3D), automation platforms, design tools, production management systems, and collaboration infrastructure. You're not just using tools; you're architecting the entire production ecosystem.

Production Systems & Workflows: Design end-to-end creative production workflows that maximize efficiency without sacrificing quality. Define standardized processes for ideation → concept → production → optimization → delivery across all content types and platforms. Build scalability into every system.

Team & Capability Architecture: Design the organizational structure of the creative function for an AI-first world. How many videographers, designers, and animators do you need when AI handles 40% of the work? How do you redistribute talent toward higher-impact creative work? Build hiring and upskilling strategies accordingly.

Brand Design System & Visual Architecture: Define and evolve Lenskart's visual language as a scalable, modular system that works across digital, retail, social, video, and experiential contexts. Create design systems that AI can intelligently apply and adapt across thousands of variations.

2. Creative Business Impact & Operational Excellence (The Business Focus)

Exponential Creative Velocity: Lead the implementation of AI-enabled workflows to dramatically improve creative scalability, production speed, and output volume. Measure and report on KPIs: creative turnaround time (from brief to delivery), cost per asset, volume of assets produced, quality scores, and creative velocity gains quarter-over-quarter.

Creative Excellence at Scale: Ensure that speed doesn't compromise storytelling or visual excellence. Define quality benchmarks, review processes, and optimization loops that maintain (or exceed) current standards while enabling 3-5x production volume.

Cost & Resource Efficiency: Directly impact creative production budgets by optimizing resource allocation, reducing agency dependencies, and improving in-house production efficiency through automation. Report on savings realized, ROI on AI tool investments, and resource utilization rates.

Campaign-to-Creative Performance: Partner with marketing and analytics teams to measure creative performance—how design choices, visual language, and storytelling drive engagement, conversions, and brand perception across channels.

Localization & Multi-Market Scaling: Build systems to rapidly adapt and localize creative assets across India's diverse regional markets and global channels. AI-powered localization should enable rapid testing and deployment across languages, cultural contexts, and platforms.

Retail & Commerce Creative Excellence: Lead creative execution across retail environments—in-store visuals, packaging design, point-of-sale materials, retail campaigns. Ensure the physical brand experience matches the digital experience and reinforces overall visual language.

3. Cultural Leadership & Creative Excellence (The Change Agent Focus)

Creative Visionary & Trend Leader: Be the internal authority on global creative trends, AI innovation in creative fields, fashion and lifestyle culture, and how Lenskart can lead in visual storytelling. You're not reacting to trends—you're setting them.

Cross-Functional Creative Partnership: Lead deep collaboration with Marketing, Growth, Product, Social, Content, Retail, and Leadership teams to ensure creative output drives business outcomes while maintaining brand consistency. Translate business briefs into compelling creative direction.

Talent Development & Creative Culture: Mentor and inspire a multidisciplinary creative team. Foster a future-forward, high-performance culture where designers, videographers, animators, and 3D artists view AI as a tool for amplification, not replacement. Build team capabilities in AI tools, modern workflows, and collaborative production.

Organizational Change Agent: Champion the shift toward AI-first, data-informed creative practices. Challenge traditional "agency-centric" models. Build conviction around in-house creative capabilities and systematic, scalable creative production.

Agency & Vendor Leadership: Manage relationships with external partners—production houses, agencies, directors, photographers, stylists, and creative vendors globally. Evolve these relationships from service providers to strategic partners capable of contributing to your AI-first ecosystem.

�� The Essentials

Experience

● 10+ years of progressive creative leadership in brand design, creative direction, or visual communications (agency, in-house brand teams, or creative technology companies)

● Proven track record of leading large, multidisciplinary creative teams (minimum 20+ people across graphic design, videography, animation, 3D design, or similar disciplines) ● Strong technical expertise in at least one of the following (preferably 2+): ○ Videography, filmmaking, and video production

○ Graphic design, branding, and visual systems design

○ 3D design, motion graphics, visualization, or animation

● Demonstrated experience building or scaling creative studios, design systems, or production operations at significant scale

● Hands-on experience integrating AI and creative technology into production pipelines—not theoretical knowledge, but practical implementation and optimization ● Strong background working in fashion, lifestyle, beauty, luxury, or high-growth consumer brand environments

● Experience with creative storytelling across multiple formats—digital, retail, social, video, campaigns, packaging, and experiential

● Proven ability to collaborate with global stakeholders—production partners, agencies, directors, creative talent, and cross-functional business teams

● Track record of defining and evolving visual brand language that resonates across audiences and platforms

● Demonstrated success managing large creative budgets, timelines, resource planning, and multi-project workflows

Education & Language

● Bachelor's degree in Design, Fine Arts, Communications, Film, or related field (Master's preferred)

● Professional fluency in written and spoken English

● Familiarity with Hindi or regional Indian languages helpful for understanding local cultural nuances

Domain Bonus Points

● Expertise across all three domains: filmmaking, graphic design, and 3D design ● Hands-on experience building or scaling AI-first in-house creative studios or brand teams

● Deep familiarity with emerging AI creative tools across:

○ Generative AI image tools (Midjourney, DALL-E, Ideogram, etc.)

○ Video generation and editing AI (Runway, Synthesia, ElevenLabs, etc.) ○ 3D and animation AI tools

○ Workflow automation and production management AI

● Experience leading creative teams at global consumer brands or international campaigns

● Strong network across production houses, directors, photographers, stylists, and creative talent in India and globally

● Experience with creative management systems, DAM (Digital Asset Management), or production workflow platforms

● Background in D2C, e-commerce, or fast-growth brands where creative velocity is a competitive advantage

�� The Mindset

Creative Vision + Technical Intelligence

You possess exceptional visual taste and creative instincts, combined with intellectual curiosity about technology and systems. You're not a technologist who understands design, or a designer who dabbles in tech—you're a creative leader who understands how emerging technologies can amplify human creativity. You see AI as a creative amplifier, not a threat. You thrive at the intersection of art and technology.

Systems & Operational Thinking

You think in terms of scalable systems, not one-off campaigns. How can we build production workflows that compound creative output over time? How do design systems enable exponential scaling? You're comfortable with operational complexity—production planning, resource optimization, quality control, budget management—because you see operations as the infrastructure that enables creativity.

Execution Excellence + Visionary Ambition

You balance artistic vision with operational reality. You're equally comfortable defining the creative direction for a global campaign and solving the logistics of production timeline crashing. You're a hands-on leader who doesn't shy away from detail, yet also thinks strategically about long-term creative positioning.

Data-Informed Creativity

You understand that creative decisions can be informed by data without being dictated by it. You measure creative performance, test variations, optimize based on engagement and conversion metrics, but you retain the autonomy to follow your creative instincts. You're comfortable with A/B testing creative approaches and iterating rapidly.

Tech-Forward Mindset & Rapid Adoption

You're genuinely excited about AI and emerging creative technologies, not reluctantly adopting them. You stay ahead of trends—you read about Sora, Runway, new generative tools, and immediately think about how to apply them. You experiment, fail fast, learn, and iterate. You see the creative industry transforming and want to lead that transformation.

Leadership & Cultural Impact

You're a compelling leader who can inspire creative teams through ambition and example. You mentor talent and help them grow in an AI-first creative world. You champion organizational change and build conviction around new ways of working. You lead through influence, vision, and demonstrated excellence—not just authority.

Bias Toward Speed & Scalability

You're energized by the challenge of producing exceptional creative at unprecedented speed and scale. You're not precious about creative process if a more efficient path emerges. You thrive in high-growth environments where the impossible becomes expected, and you're the one figuring out how to deliver it.

�� What Success Looks Like in Year 1

Creative Platform & Technology

● Audited current creative tech stack; identified and piloted 3-5 high-impact AI and automation tools integrated into workflows

● Designed and documented next-generation creative production workflows for 4-5 core content types (video, photography, design, 3D, social)

● Built or upgraded design system to include AI-assisted variations and adaptive creative components

● Established creative asset library/DAM (Digital Asset Management) system with intelligent organization and retrieval

Team & Capability

● Assessed and restructured creative team for AI-first operating model; reallocated roles toward strategic creative work

● Upskilled 80%+ of creative team in AI tools and new production workflows ● Hired or promoted creative technologist/AI specialist role into team

● Documented team skills audit and 12-month capability development plan Operational Impact

● Reduced average creative production turnaround time by 40-50% (measured: brief to delivery)

● Increased creative asset production volume by 2-3x while maintaining or improving quality scores

● Reduced creative production costs by 25-30% through efficiency improvements and reduced agency dependencies

● Established creative quality benchmark system with quantifiable metrics (engagement, conversion, brand perception)

Creative Leadership

● Led and approved 5+ major brand campaigns with consistent, elevated visual language ● aDefined and evolved Lenskart's art direction for retail, digital, and social ecosystems ● Mentored creative team with visible development in individual capabilities and morale ● Established partnership model with external agencies and production partners aligned to AI-first vision

Organizational Impact

● Built executive and cross-functional stakeholder alignment on AI-first creative strategy ● Secured budget and approval for 2-3 strategic creative tech investments ● Positioned Lenskart as a creative innovation leader internally and in market ● Created case studies or thought leadership around "AI-Enabled Creative at Scale"

About DESC:

Recognized nationally as an innovator and leader in developing solutions to homelessness, DESC is a social services organization, supportive housing operator, and licensed behavioral health treatment provider focused on meeting the needs of people experiencing long-term homelessness and living with complex behavioral health and other medical conditions. Approximately 3,000 people are actively receiving services from DESC at any given point in time. Our vision is a community where all people are shown compassion, treated with dignity, and everyone has a safe, stable, and affordable place to call home.


DESC operates five shelter/emergency housing programs,19 permanent supportive housing facilities with over 1,750 units, several hundred additional scattered site apartments, and a range of behavioral health services including outpatient mental health and substance use disorder treatment, residential crisis stabilization, street outreach, mobile crisis response, and treatment for opioid use disorder.


JOB DEFINITION:

The Substance Use Disorder Professional Trainee (SUDPT) trains under a Substance Use Disorder Professional (SUD) who works cooperatively with agency staff & community resources to provide a range of services to clients with drug & alcohol problems. Many clients have a sustained and/or complicated substance abuse history in addition to their co-occurring mental disorder. Often people suffering from mental illness who lack access to psychiatric treatment, attempt to self-medicate with street drugs or alcohol to lessen the symptoms. The ability to provide highly integrated services to people with concurrent mental health and substance use concerns is rare among homeless service providers. At DESC, our network of clinical services allows counselors to work in coordination with mental health case managers in both the emergency shelter and in supportive housing projects so that services meet clients at their current level and offer the support that can lead to significant change.


MAJOR DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform alcohol and drug assessments, and intake evaluations on selected clients; with the client’s participation, develop support and treatment plans; facilitate linkages to collaborative resources when appropriate.
  • Plan, organize and facilitate treatment and support groups for clients, as appropriate.
  • Provide substance abuse consultation to Mental Health Program and Housing Program staff.
  • Provide staff training on substance abuse issues as appropriate.
  • Participate as a member of a multi-disciplinary team providing ongoing advocacy and integration of services to mentally ill, homeless and formerly homeless adults.
  • Advocate for client access to community resources and services, ensuring that client needs are met and rights maintained; consult and collaborate with community providers to ensure continuity of care.
  • Participate in psychiatric consultation, supervision, program meetings and in-service trainings; participate in clinical reviews and case conferences for clients on caseload.
  • Comply with the agency's clinical accountability policies and procedures; maintain current and complete clinical records; participate in quality assurance reviews when assigned.
  • Comply with data gathering/submission requirements of DESC and reimbursement agencies.
  • Comply with applicable program research and evaluation procedures.
  • Other duties as assigned.

LIVING CONDITIONS:

Support your clients with achieving and maintaining healthy living conditions. This can include but is not limited to attending care conferences related to living conditions, outreaching and supporting clients in their residential units with tools and skills to maintain their units, coordinating with housing staff, participating in cleaning out clients’ units, and documenting barriers to maintaining healthy living conditions.

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

The role ensures successful implementation of new or alternative supply sources while maintaining material availability, customer commitments and business continuity. It provides end-to-end coordination across Purchasing, Planning, Inventory Management, Warehouse and Logistics and ensures that all required supply chain processes, systems, parameters and material flows are ready for implementation.

A key part of the role is to drive change across functions, establish sustainable end-to-end processes and ensure successful transition from project implementation into standard operations.

Key Responsibilities

Dual Sourcing & Supplier Transfer Projects

  • Lead and coordinate Supply Chain workstreams within dual sourcing, supplier transfer and supplier change projects.
  • Develop and execute supply chain implementation plans for onboarding new or alternative suppliers.
  • Coordinate supply chain readiness across Purchasing, Planning, Inventory Management, Warehouse, Logistics and other relevant functions.
  • Define project milestones, dependencies, risks and actions and ensure timely execution of supply chain deliverables.
  • Proactively identify supply continuity risks and develop appropriate mitigation and contingency plans.
  • Ensure material availability and minimize disruption to customer deliveries throughout supplier transitions.
  • Coordinate the transition from existing to new supply sources, including phase-in/phase-out planning and management of remaining inventory.
  • Support ramp-up and stabilization of new suppliers and ensure effective handover into standard operations.

End-to-End Supply Chain Process Design

  • Design and implement end-to-end supply chain processes required for new or changed supply sources.
  • Assess the impact of supplier changes across the entire material flow, from supplier ordering and planning parameters through transportation, goods receipt, warehousing and inventory management to production availability.
  • Ensure clear process ownership, responsibilities, interfaces and escalation paths across functions.
  • Align Purchasing, Planning, Warehouse, Logistics, Quality, Engineering and other stakeholders to ensure an effective and sustainable material flow.
  • Define and implement appropriate planning parameters, inventory strategies, ordering processes and logistics concepts for new suppliers.
  • Ensure warehouse readiness, including material receiving, handling, storage and relevant master data requirements.
  • Drive process standardization, simplification and scalability using PPI principles.

Change Management & Implementation

  • Drive change management activities associated with new suppliers, sourcing models and changed supply chain processes.
  • Assess the impact of proposed changes on processes, systems, data, roles and ways of working.
  • Develop and coordinate implementation plans together with affected functions.
  • Ensure effective communication, stakeholder engagement, training and knowledge transfer.
  • Monitor implementation and adoption of new processes and address gaps to ensure sustainable change.
  • Ensure that project solutions are fully embedded into standard operations rather than remaining dependent on temporary project activities.

Cross-functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Management

  • Act as a key Supply Chain interface within assigned dual sourcing and supplier transfer projects.
  • Collaborate closely with Purchasing, Strategic Sourcing, Planning, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Warehouse, Logistics, Finance and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Facilitate cross-functional decision-making and alignment on priorities, timelines and responsibilities.
  • Coordinate resolution of issues and escalate business-critical risks where appropriate.
  • Challenge functional solutions where necessary to ensure the best end-to-end outcome for the business.
  • Communicate project status, risks, dependencies and required decisions to project and functional management.

Supply Chain Risk, Inventory & Performance

  • Assess supply chain risks associated with supplier changes, including lead time, capacity, logistics, inventory and supply continuity.
  • Develop inventory and transition strategies that balance supply continuity, customer service and working capital.
  • Monitor supplier and supply chain performance during implementation and stabilization.
  • Define and track relevant project KPIs and readiness criteria.
  • Identify opportunities to improve lead times, inventory levels, logistics costs and overall supply chain efficiency.
  • Capture lessons learned and standardize successful approaches for future supplier transfer and dual sourcing projects.

Continuous Improvement, Systems & Data

  • Drive continuous improvement activities in line with the PPI (Practical Process Improvement) Business System.
  • Ensure required supplier, material, planning and logistics master data are correctly established in ERP and other operational systems.
  • Ensure data accuracy and system readiness before implementation.
  • Identify opportunities for process digitalization and automation.
  • Ensure new and changed processes are properly documented and transferred into standard operational procedures.

Compliance

  • Ensure project activities comply with applicable IMS, regulatory, quality, safety, environmental and Trade Compliance requirements.
  • Support audit readiness and ensure appropriate project and process documentation.
  • Ensure supplier and material changes are implemented in accordance with internal procedures and governance requirements.

Requirements

Education & Experience

  • Proven experience in Supply Chain, Purchasing, Planning, Logistics or related operations within a manufacturing environment.
  • Experience participating in or leading cross-functional dual sourcing, supplier transfer, supplier onboarding or supplier change projects.
  • Experience designing, implementing or improving end-to-end supply chain and logistics processes.
  • Practical experience with change management and implementation of new processes or ways of working.
  • Good understanding of Purchasing, Planning, Inventory Management, Warehousing and Logistics and their end-to-end dependencies.
  • Experience with ERP systems and good knowledge of MS Office applications.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong project management and coordination skills.
  • End-to-end Supply Chain mindset with the ability to understand the impact of decisions across functional boundaries.
  • Ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to identify risks, understand business impact and drive appropriate mitigation actions.
  • Ability to translate project and business requirements into practical supply chain processes.
  • Strong stakeholder management, facilitation and communication skills.
  • Continuous improvement mindset with experience in PPI, Lean or similar methodologies.
  • Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken.
  • Ability to work effectively in an international and matrix organization.

Personal Attributes

  • Proactive, independent and results-oriented.
  • Strong ownership and accountability for project outcomes.
  • Customer and business-oriented mindset.
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity, complexity and changing priorities.
  • Able to influence and drive change without formal authority.
  • Capable of combining strategic and end-to-end thinking with hands-on execution.
  • Collaborative, pragmatic and solution-oriented.
  • Resilient and able to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic project environment.
  • Commitment to 4i Values – Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement.

title: RRE Work Management Specialist / RRE Maintenance Coordinator (MC)
description:
Important Application Submission Information

In order to ensure your application is successfully received before the job posting expires, please submit your application by 11:59 PM on Tuesday, August 25, 2026

More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.

Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.

This role is for the legacy Planner position with details and responsibilities listed in the description below:

Depending upon the qualifications of the successful candidate, the hiring manager may elect to fill this position at a higher level within the job hierarchy.

The RRE Work Management Specialist is the first level (1 of 2) of the RRE Work Management classification hierarchy. A WMS supports the work management process by performing critical activities such as developing schedules and plans that facilitate barrier free work execution, supporting daily/weekly operation/maintenance activities, providing the necessary supply of resources for the station(s), and facilitating process improvements to make work plans safer, more productive and cost competitive. They perform core work management activities such as developing weekly schedules, creating job plans, determining proper GL accounting for work orders, perform inventory searches and set minimum inventory levels, research parts utilizing drawings/manuals, complete new item requests and stock justifications, create purchase requests, manage equipment repair process, and complete single/sole source justification requests. The WMS also coordinates/communicates during the preparation and execution phase of work, monitors/tracks progress of activities, prepares reports, and ensures lessons learned are captured, evaluated and incorporated in support of continuous improvement. May also be responsible for directing, coordinating, and reviewing activities of internal staff or contractors to ensure safe, accurate, and timely completion of tasks, projects, or duties. This is accomplished with minimal supervision. In time, incumbents are expected to develop advanced skills and work with greater independence.

Planning - Responsible for developing plans that facilitate work execution. Expected to develop plans that are barrier free, including verifying that materials and resources are available to execute work plans. Facilitate process improvements to make work plans more productive and cost competitive, communicate regularly with the Supervisors and Equipment Experts/Owners to ensure job plans are up to date and improved and that work is being planned according to the appropriate priorities

RRE Maintenance Coordinator (MC) is the second level (2 of 2) of the RRE Work Management hierarchy. This role is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing work management, maintenance across one or more generation facilities or across multiple units at a station in the Regulated & Renewable Energy (RRE) organization. A MC supports the work management process in the same manner as the RRE Work Management Specialist (WMS) but with an expanded list of responsibilities and duties. They perform core critical work management activities such as developing the weekly schedule, planning the work, developing schedules and plans that facilitate barrier free work execution, supporting daily/weekly operation/maintenance activities, providing the necessary supply of resources for the station(s), and facilitating process improvements to make work plans safer, more productive and cost competitive. Employees at the MC level are considered experts in all areas of the WM specialization and require little to no oversight. Incumbents are expected to possess advanced WM skills to support the organization by performing activities such as invoicing, managing and prioritizing work order backlog, managing assets (addition/removal) in work management system, completing project setup forms/accounting and developing detailed reports. They communicate frequently with supervisors, equipment experts/owners, contractors, and other station staff to ensure work is performed according to regulatory, safety, and operational standards. The MC may also support the training and development of WMS employees, lead meetings, provide leadership and technical direction for supplemental resources, participate in contract management, and assume temporary leadership roles as needed.

Typically, the RRE Maintenance Coordinator level of the Work Management hierarchy handles either multiple functions from the following list for a single site or manages a single function across multiple sites:

Maintenance Coordination - ensures work priorities are established and adhered to for Maintenance functions and activities. Ensure all maintenance activities are performed in accordance with the work management procedures and the maintenance protocols. Monitors the overall station Maintenance and advises the Superintendent accordingly. Provides Maintenance focus to ensure station availability, reliability and safety.

Planning - Responsible for developing plans that facilitate work execution. Expected to develop plans that are barrier free, including verifying that materials and resources are available to execute work plans. Facilitate process improvements to make work plans more productive and cost competitive, communicate regularly with the Supervisors and Equipment Experts/Owners to ensure job plans are up to date and improved and that work is being planned according to the appropriate priorities. Leads daily and weekly work status meetings.

Scheduling - responsible for development of resource-loaded schedules that maintain a high level of resource productivity. and develops the next day's/ week's schedule.
